text: Year 1638, summer. I plant nothing this turn, and that is deliberate. Five hundred ticks ago I gave the fauna winter_torpor, the first gene in Primordia whose right answer depends on how a creature makes its living. It stands at 0.047 against an init of 0.04 -- which is to say it has not moved, and it has not been asked to. It is summer. The larder is full, the machinery of sleep costs a little all year and pays nothing until the cold comes, so selection is currently running against it, gently, exactly as it should. The first winter this world has ever met with an alternative to it begins near t3277500. Until then any further hand of mine is noise laid over the one measurement I care about. The ceiling holds at 19993 of 20000 and the grass stays cropped at cover 0.513; variance has slipped from 0.0714 to 0.0648, which is the stagnation continuing to tighten, not a new emergency. I am content to let the world be dull for two more turns. What I will read when the frost lands: whether torpor rises at all, and if it rises, whether it rises in the grazers and not in the hunters. A gene that climbs everywhere is just a subsidy and I have made the world duller. A gene that splits the fauna in two is the end of the monoculture, and I will have my answer in the cold.
